question:
A 1-month-old male infant with no prior health issues is evaluated for feeding difficulties lasting 10
days, accompanied by respiratory distress and diaphoresis during feeds. The patient was delivered
vaginally at 38 weeks without prenatal care, with birth measurements of 51 cm length and 3660 g
weight. Initial Apgar scores were 8 and 9, and the newborn examination was unremarkable, leading to
discharge at 2 days of age. Current examination reveals growth at the 20th percentile for length and
10th percentile for weight. Vital signs show temperature 36°C, heart rate 190/min, respiratory rate
37/min, and blood pressure 87/57 mm Hg. Room air oxygen saturation is 96% with labored breathing.
Physical examination reveals a grade 2/6 holosystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border without
cyanosis. ECG demonstrates left-axis deviation, while chest x-ray shows left atrial and ventricular
enlargement with increased pulmonary vascularity. Doppler echocardiography confirms an intracardiac
shunt. Which physiologic change most likely contributed to the development of the patient's current
clinical presentation? Answer Choices: (A) Closure of the ductus arteriosus (B) Increase in systemic
vascular resistance (C) Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction (D) Development of pulmonary venous
congestion (E) Increased left-to-right shunting due to septal defect enlargement (F) Decreased
systemic cardiac output (G) Failure of physiologic cardiac remodeling (H) Decrease in pulmonary
vascular resistance (I) Progressive right ventricular hypertrophy (J) Persistent pulmonary hypertension
 A. Closure of the ductus arteriosus
B. Failure of physiologic cardiac remodeling
C. Progressive right ventricular hypertrophy
D. Decrease in pulmonary vascular resistance
E. Persistent pulmonary hypertension
F. Increase in systemic vascular resistance
G. Increased left-to-right shunting due to septal defect enlargement
H. Decreased systemic cardiac output
I. Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction
J. Development of pulmonary venous congestion
